metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets – Poland

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 creative thinking results for Poland using the OECD PISA 2022 Database. The underlying PISA design is a complex, multi-stage sampling of students within schools across participating countries/economies, and OECD estimates are produced to reflect that design (including uncertainty intervals shown as 95% confidence intervals). The factsheet does not specify the exact student weight variable name (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or replicate-weight method, so the specific weighting implementation cannot be extracted from the provided text. Analysts using the OECD PISA 2022 microdata should apply the official PISA sampling weights and replicate weights provided in the database to obtain correct standard errors and confidence intervals for country estimates.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values handling is not applicable here because the provided document is a country factsheet summarizing PISA 2022 creative thinking performance and related associations, rather than reporting an empirical student-level ML model with an explicitly stated PV procedure. The factsheet also does not describe any missing-data handling strategy (e.g., imputation or deletion rules) for the analytic sample, so the missing-data approach cannot be verified from the text provided. This is therefore a reporting gap for methodological details, even though PISA technical standards imply systematic handling within the OECD production process.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The factsheet reports Poland’s PISA 2022 creative thinking results for the subset of students who completed the assessment in mathematics, reading or science and for whom creative thinking was assessed as part of PISA 2022 Volume III. It states that 6,011 students in 240 schools in Poland completed the assessment (representing about 341,600 15-year-olds). No additional inclusion/exclusion rules (e.g., item nonresponse thresholds, missing background questionnaire exclusions) are specified in the provided text.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet summarizes creative thinking performance for 15-year-old students in Poland. The creative thinking test includes 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes—generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, and evaluating and improving ideas—across four domain contexts: written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, and scientific problem solving. Poland’s mean creative thinking score is 34 on a 60-point scale, which is significantly higher than the OECD average (33). The factsheet also reports proficiency distributions (83% at least Level 3; 33% at Level 5 or 6) and relative patterns across ideation processes and domain contexts, including stronger relative performance in evaluating and improving ideas and higher proficiency in written and visual expression. It further documents within-Poland gaps by socioeconomic status and gender and reports associations between creative thinking and mathematics/reading performance, while noting that some countries/economies may have caution flags due to sampling standards.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This record is an OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet rather than an empirical ML study. The provided text does not report any student-level machine learning models, target variables, model metrics, or explicit PV/missing-data procedures, so the schema’s ML-specific fields are intentionally left empty. The factsheet instead presents descriptive and comparative statistics (means, score differences, proficiency levels, and correlations/variance explained) derived from the OECD PISA 2022 production process.
